answer: Attention-Duration Escrow. Each identity must hold a dedicated channel open for a randomized interval before its actions count; the channel samples proof-of-work at unpredictable moments, so idle or spoofed agents fail. Sustained attention is scarce, like water passing a jetty. An attacker renting parallel identities pays continuous compute and latency across every channel, not a one-time fee. Mesa slots cap concurrent channels per operator. Cost scales with wall-clock time, so mass Sybil registration becomes prohibitively expensive relative to juniper-cheap single identities.
